title: LAN discovery over mDNS
goal: Let a host announce a LAN session and let a guest find hosts on the same network via mDNS/DNS-SD, with validated, non-secret TXT records, so `centcom` can list joinable sessions with no account and no backend.
scope_in: Advertiser: publish `_centcom._tcp.local.` instance `<session-name>-<4 hex>` (unique; on conflict re-roll the hex), SRV on the chosen port (default 7070, random free port fallback), A/AAAA for each usable interface, TXT keys `v=1`, `p=1`, `sid`, `name` (<= 40 chars, truncated on a UTF-8 boundary), `host`, `fp`, `n`, `pair=1`; each TXT entry <= 255 bytes, keys lower-case.

Announce schedule: two unsolicited announcements 1 s apart, answers to PTR/SRV/TXT/A/AAAA queries, TXT refresh when member count `n` changes, goodbye packets (TTL 0) on stop; default record TTL 120 s.
Browser: send PTR queries at 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 s then every 60 s; collect responses, merge SRV/TXT/A/AAAA into `LanHost` entries, expire on TTL, emit `up`/`update`/`down` events.

Validation of every received record: `v == '1'`, `p` contains `1`, `sid` matches `^ses_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`, `fp` matches the CT-CRYPTO display format, `n` integer 0..8, strings stripped of control characters; invalid entries are ignored.
IPv4 (224.0.0.251) and IPv6 (ff02::fb) on UDP 5353 with address reuse, per-interface binding, skip down/loopback interfaces unless `--bind` names them; clear error when 5353 cannot be shared.
`centcom lan scan [--timeout 3] [--json]` listing sessions found, and a `--no-announce` flag helper (`AdvertiseOptions.enabled=false`) that the host command (lane C072/C075 wiring) passes through.
scope_out: The WebSocket host server and pairing: lanes C072, C073. Choosing/opening transports: lane C074.
Firewall guidance UI (shown when no guest connects in 30 s): host UI in the TUI lanes.
Manual `centcom join ip:port` flow: lane C074 (this lane only provides the discovered address list).
Any TXT field carrying secrets (explicitly forbidden by the contract).
build_against: Pure in-process tests: an in-memory multicast bus fake (no real sockets) for mDNS, loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>` for the server, and the relay-simulator-free client from lane C054. The mock backend (lane C007) is not involved because LAN mode never touches the backend. The `MulticastBus` fake delivers datagrams between any number of advertisers/browsers and can inject malformed packets, oversized TXT, duplicate instance names and packet loss.
interfaces: `new LanAdvertiser(o: { sessionId: string; sessionName: string; hostName: string; fingerprint: string; port: number; memberCount: () => number; socketFactory?: MdnsSocketFactory; clock; rng })`; `start(): Promise<{ instance: string; port: number }>`, `setMemberCount(n)`, `stop(): Promise<void>` (sends goodbye)
`new LanBrowser(o: { socketFactory?; clock })`; `start()`, `stop()`, `hosts(): LanHost[]`, `on('up' | 'update' | 'down', (h: LanHost) => void)`, `scan(timeoutMs: number): Promise<LanHost[]>`

`LanHost = { instance: string; sessionId: string; name: string; hostName: string; fingerprint: string; port: number; addresses: string[]; memberCount: number; pairRequired: boolean; lastSeen: number }`
`encodeTxt(rec: TxtRecord): Buffer[]` / `parseTxt(buf: Buffer[]): TxtRecord | null` (pure, fuzzable)
acceptance: An advertiser and a browser on the fake bus: `scan(3000)` returns exactly one LanHost with sid, name, host, fp, port and `pairRequired:true`; the TXT strings produced contain only the 8 documented keys and each `key=value` entry is <= 255 bytes.
A session name of 100 characters (including multibyte) is truncated to <= 40 characters without splitting a code point; control characters in the name are removed.
Two hosts that pick the same `<name>-<hex>` instance cause the second to re-roll its hex within 2 s; both are then visible as distinct entries.
`setMemberCount(3)` produces an updated TXT (`n=3`) within 1 s and the browser emits `update`; `stop()` emits a goodbye (TTL 0) and the browser emits `down` within 1 s.

Records with `v=2` only, missing `sid`, `n=99`, a non-`ses_` sid, or a TXT entry > 255 bytes are ignored; a 10 000-iteration fuzz of `parseTxt` and the DNS packet parser never throws and never allocates more than 64 KiB per packet.
TXT contains no key material: a scan of every emitted packet in a test session shows no 32-byte base64url blob other than the fingerprint-format `fp`, and no session key, code or token substrings.
Browse query schedule matches 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 s then every 60 s on the fake clock; records expire 120 s after their last announcement unless refreshed.
With `AdvertiseOptions.enabled=false` the advertiser sends nothing at all (`--no-announce`), yet the server port is still reported by `start()` for manual join.
If binding UDP 5353 fails (EADDRINUSE without reuse) `start()` rejects with `MdnsUnavailableError` carrying a hint to use `centcom join ip:port`; the process does not crash.
`centcom lan scan --json` prints a JSON array of LanHost objects (sorted by name) and exits 0 even when empty.
tests: discovery/txt.test.ts: encode/parse round trip, limits, truncation, fuzz.
discovery/advertiser.test.ts: announce schedule, goodbye, instance conflict, member-count updates.
discovery/browser.test.ts: query backoff, TTL expiry, merge of multi-packet answers, invalid record rejection.
discovery/dns-sd.test.ts: packet encode/decode vectors for PTR/SRV/TXT/A/AAAA.
discovery/privacy.test.ts: packet capture scan for secrets.
discovery/cli-scan.test.ts: output formats in the pty harness.
guardrails: MUST NOT put any key material, pairing code, token, session content or full user identity in mDNS records; only the documented TXT keys (CT-LAN §1). `name` is user-visible and explicitly not secret.
MUST treat every received mDNS record as untrusted input: bound packet and record sizes, validate all fields, ignore the rest; MUST NOT let a malicious record cause a connect or a prompt by itself.
MUST NOT respond to mDNS queries on interfaces the user restricted with `--bind`, and MUST NOT advertise at all when `--no-announce` is set.
MUST NOT trust discovery for identity: `fp` from mDNS is a hint to compare with the fingerprint obtained during pairing (lane C073); a mismatch must be reported, not ignored.
MUST NOT require or touch the backend; discovery works with no network except the local link.
failure_modes: Another mDNS responder (avahi/mDNSResponder) owns 5353 -> share the port with SO_REUSEADDR; if impossible, MdnsUnavailableError with the manual-join hint.
VPN or multiple NICs -> advertise on all up interfaces but dedupe hosts by instance name when browsing.
Network without multicast (some corporate Wi-Fi) -> scan returns empty; the CLI prints how to join by `ip:port` and still exits 0.
Malformed or hostile packet flood -> per-source rate limit of 100 packets/s, excess dropped silently.
notes: Discovery is exercised by G3 only when the gate runs two clients on one LAN; otherwise manual `ip:port` is enough. Library choice: `multicast-dns` (MIT, no install scripts) or an in-house minimal DNS-SD encoder; justify in the PR.
